name: 993 AD Miyake Event

phenomena.details: ~9‰ Δ14C spike in global tree rings; second largest known cosmogenic isotope event after 774 AD.

impacts.description: High-energy particle bombardment of the atmosphere inferred from cosmogenic isotope records; likely caused significant ionospheric disturbance.

papers.title: Another rapid event in the carbon-14 content of tree rings
papers.authors: Miyake, F., Masuda, K., Nakamura, T.
papers.keyFinding: Identified a second rapid 14C increase (~9‰) at AD 993–994, establishing that extreme solar particle events recur on timescales of centuries.

summary: A second major cosmogenic isotope spike at AD 993–994, roughly three-quarters the magnitude of the 774 event, demonstrates that solar particle events of extreme intensity are not unique occurrences in the Holocene.
description: Analysis of tree-ring 14C records published by Miyake et al. in 2013 revealed a rapid increase of ~9‰ in Δ14C spanning AD 993–994, later confirmed in multiple tree-ring chronologies from the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. The event is approximately 75% the magnitude of the 774 AD event and similarly requires a very large SEP fluence to explain the observed isotope production. The existence of two such events within ~220 years suggests these extreme solar particle storms may occur once or twice per millennium. No contemporary aurora reports or other written records have been unambiguously connected to this event.
